This issue affects Apache Tomcat: from 11.0.0-M1 through 11.0.27, from 10.1.0-M1 through 10.1.61, from 9.0.0.M1 through 9.0.123.



The following versions were EOL at the time the CVE was created but are known to be affected: from 8.5.0 through 8.5.100, from 7.0.0 through 7.0.109. Other unsupported versions may also be affected.



Users are recommended to upgrade to version 11.0.29, 10.1.62 or 9.0.124, which fixes the issue.
Note: Tomcat 11.0.28 was not released

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-133306
CVE.report.description: VideoLAN libaacs 0.7.0 through 0.12.0 on non-macOS, non-Windows builds contains stack-based buffer overflows in aacs_resolve_path() in src/file/path.c from length checks against the wrong buffer. Local attackers can place a symlink with a long target on a disc path a user opens to overflow resolved_path[] and link[], crashing the process or potentially executing code if mitigations are bypassed.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-132607
CVE.report.description:
Insufficient verification of data authenticity in the decryption component of Amazon S3 Encryption Client for PHP in AWS SDK for PHP before 3.383.1 might allow an authenticated remote user to forge ciphertext that decrypts to arbitrary plaintext via manipulation of the GCM authentication tag length metadata.



To remediate this issue, users should upgrade to AWS SDK for PHP version 3.383.1 or later.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131305
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk AI Assistant versions below 2.0.0, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could submit client-controlled feature settings through the Representational State Transfer (REST) API. This could modify limited response metadata outside the expected server-side configuration.
The vulnerability is possible because the REST API processes client-supplied feature settings without enforcing the expected server-side configuration boundary.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131295
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to create and run playbooks could start child playbooks on containers outside the authorized label, or repository scope for that user. This could expose container data and affect automation outside that scope.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not bind the identity used to authorize the child playbook run to the parent playbook execution context.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131293
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to edit and run playbooks could read or overwrite persisted data for playbook runs outside the authorized label, or ownership scope for that user. The affected data can include playbook inputs, prompt and block results, outputs, and secrets that playbooks save in run data. Overwriting the data could corrupt results that paused, scheduled, or parent playbook runs later use.
The vulnerability is possible because the playbook automation APIs do not bind data operations to the active playbook run.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131291
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a Splunk SOAR user who can edit and run playbooks for a permitted container label could associate action and callback state with a running playbook outside that container label. This could affect playbook automation for containers that the user cannot view.
The vulnerability is possible because the Playbook Automation API accepts a supplied playbook run identifier without verifying that it is bound to the server-provided playbook execution context.
The vulnerability requires a running playbook on a container label that the user cannot view.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131288
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with access to the configured load balancer account could replace a load balancer helper that Splunk SOAR later runs with root privileges during cluster lifecycle operations. If a Splunk SOAR administrator performs a cluster lifecycle operation, Splunk SOAR could execute arbitrary code with root privileges on the load balancer.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not verify the integrity or ownership of the load balancer helper before running it with root privileges.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131287
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the Playbooks view, edit, execute, and delete permissions could cause existing cross-repository playbook references to run attacker-controlled playbook code.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR can bind existing cross-repository playbook references to a different source control repository when a deleted repository name is reused.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131286
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user with permission to author and run playbooks could view action data outside the authorized scope for that user and change the status and message of another playbook run.
The vulnerability is possible because the playbook API does not verify that the requested playbook run is within the authorized scope of the authenticated user.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131282
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user who holds the "Observer" Splunk SOAR role could access a password-reset credential in a diagnostic log bundle and reset the password for an active local account.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not redact password-reset email bodies before it logs communications between product processes.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131278
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user with local access to the affected host could obtain a live Splunk SOAR session token or decrypted asset configuration when another user starts an App Editor debug action.
The vulnerability is possible because App Editor debug actions expose sensitive runtime information to other local users on the affected host.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131272
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission could use the Automation Dependency Wheel Representational State Transfer (REST) API to write arbitrary files outside the intended directory, which could lead to arbitrary code execution.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not restrict uploaded automation dependency wheel filenames to the intended storage directory.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131268
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission could use a customer automation dependency to execute arbitrary code as the user account that runs Splunk SOAR.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not properly separate customer automation dependencies from trusted product code.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131263
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with only the apps:edit permission could install a connector app that causes Splunk SOAR to write attacker-controlled files outside the app directory. This could let the user modify files used by Splunk SOAR and execute arbitrary code as the user account that runs Splunk SOAR.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR constructs the dependency installation command from app-supplied metadata without preventing that metadata from changing its arguments.
For more information see Manage roles and permissions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.8.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-users-and-accounts/manage-roles-and-permissions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) and Add and configure apps and assets to provide actions in Splunk SOAR (On-premises) (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-soar/soar-on-premises/administer-soar-on-premises/8.6.0/manage-your-splunk-soar-on-premises-apps-and-assets/add-and-configure-apps-and-assets-to-provide-actions-in-splunk-soar-on-premises) in the Splunk documentation.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131261
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, a user that holds a role with the Apps edit permission could execute arbitrary code as the user account that runs Splunk SOAR by installing a malicious app.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk SOAR does not restrict app dependencies to validated binary packages before installing them.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131256
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user that holds a role with the System Settings edit permission could execute arbitrary code on the host that runs Splunk SOAR.
The vulnerability is possible because the Representational State Transfer (REST) API accepts package references from untrusted sources and passes them to the dependency installer.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131255
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an unauthenticated user could gain administrator privileges through a user account that receives an unintended role. A user that holds a role with permission to create or modify users and assign roles must assign the target account a role with a numeric name through the user-management Representational State Transfer (REST) API.
The vulnerability is possible because the API resolves a numeric role name as a role identifier instead of preserving the requested role name.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131253
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk SOAR versions below 8.8.0, an authenticated user that holds a role with the Apps edit, Containers edit, and Playbooks execute permissions could use the App Wizard to execute arbitrary code as the user account that runs Splunk SOAR. This could compromise the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the Splunk SOAR instance.
The vulnerability exists because the App Wizard does not validate user-supplied identifiers before incorporating them into generated connector code.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131202
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk Enterprise Security versions below 8.7.0, a user who holds the "ess_admin" Splunk Enterprise Security role could execute arbitrary code on the search head as the user account running Splunk Enterprise by combining lookup file upload and Configuration Checker functionality.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise Security does not restrict lookup upload file types or keep Configuration Checker module paths within the intended directory.
For more information see Users and roles for Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/install/8.7/installation/users-and-roles-for-splunk-enterprise-security) and Create and manage lookups in Splunk Enterprise Security (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise-security-8/administer/8.7/managing-security-content/create-and-manage-lookups-in-splunk-enterprise-security) in the Splunk documentation.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131194
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.4, 10.2.8, 10.0.11, and 9.4.16, a low-privileged user who holds the "power" Splunk role could inject malicious content into a Splunk Web view. When another authenticated user opens the affected view in Splunk Web, the injected content executes unauthorized JavaScript code within the viewing user's browser session.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Web does not properly validate content in a view definition before rendering the view.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.2/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131184
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a low-privileged user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could inject a malicious script into the name of a private saved search. If another user subsequently enables, disables, or edits the corresponding platform alert in the Monitoring Console, the injected script executes within that user's browser session, potentially allowing the low-privileged user to view sensitive information or modify data in Splunk Enterprise.
The vulnerability is possible because the Monitoring Console does not safely handle saved-search names in the platform alert workflow.
For more information see Enable and configure platform alerts (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/monitor/10.4/configure-the-monitoring-console/enable-and-configure-platform-alerts) and About configuring role-based user access (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/about-configuring-role-based-user-access) in the Splunk documentation.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131179
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could add attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) to a shared dashboard. When another user opens the dashboard in Splunk Web, Splunk Enterprise could run the attacker-controlled SPL using the permissions of that dashboard viewer. The attacker-controlled SPL could expose stored credentials, modify indexed data, and reduce availability.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not neutralize special elements in search filter values before it builds optimized search jobs.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the affected user by tricking them into initiating a request within their browser. The attacker should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131174
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could make unauthorized changes when restoring archived indexed data or cause a Denial of Service (DoS) on the Splunk Enterprise instance.
The vulnerability is possible because the Representational State Transfer (REST) API does not require the indexes_edit capability for archived-data restoration actions.
For more information see Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.6/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities) in the Splunk documentation.
For more information see Restore archived indexed data (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-indexers-and-indexer-clusters/10.6/back-up-and-archive-your-indexes/restore-archived-indexed-data) in the Splunk documentation.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130236
CVE.report.description: In the Auth0 Authorization Extension, request authentication handling can process claims from query parameters independently of header validation. Under specific preconditions, this may allow an authenticated tenant user to issue requests to the extension's administrative endpoints. Also, input handling during rule generation may permit modification of the tenant login rule published by the extension.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130161
CVE.report.description: Tamari is a fully-featured recipe manager web application built using Python and the Flask Framework. Prior to 1.7.2, an authenticated user can bypass the recipe-autofill SSRF check by submitting a hostname under the user's control through the Autofill from URL feature; the hostname can resolve to a public address during validation and a private or internal address during the later connection. In app/myrecipes/routes.py, is_safe_autofill_url validates the first DNS response, but recipe autofill passes the original URL to requests.get, which independently resolves the hostname and can connect to the internal address. The fetched response is parsed into recipe fields, enabling internal-service reconnaissance and potential data exposure; no redirect is required, and disabling redirects does not stop this DNS-rebinding bypass. This issue is fixed in 1.7.2.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-126765
CVE.report.description:
The glob functions in the GNU C Library versions 2.44 and earlier may free the same heap block twice when a memory allocation fails while glob prepends the directory name to the names it matched.  The names already rewritten are freed, but their pointers stay in the result vector, and the error path frees them again with globfree.

The allocation must fail after at least one name has been rewritten, so the issue can only be reached when the process is already close to its memory limit, for example under an address space limit (RLIMIT_AS) or on a 32-bit system.  The attacker needs control to make the result large enough to make the program or service run out of memory, either by controlling the glob pattern and having knowledge of the filesystem layout or through other means.  This issue affects all architectures and ABIs supported by the GNU C Library.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-87977
CVE.report.description: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to SQL injection in the edge-controller component. An unauthenticated remote attacker could exploit this vulnerability to access or modify sensitive database information.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-85018
CVE.report.description: IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 is vulnerable to improper TLS certificate validation in the GDP Terraform provider, allowing a network attacker with a man-in-the-middle position to intercept sensitive credentials transmitted to the Guardium appliance.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-76543
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.6.1, 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17, a user who holds the "power" Splunk role could store attacker-controlled Search Processing Language (SPL) in a shared data model.
The vulnerability is possible because the Data Model Editor does not properly neutralize data model field names when it builds a preview search.
The vulnerability requires the attacker to phish the affected user by tricking them into initiating a request within their browser. The attacker should not be able to exploit the vulnerability at will.
For more information see Add a regular expression field (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/manage-knowledge-objects/knowledge-management-manual/10.4/define-data-model-dataset-fields/add-a-regular-expression-field), Define roles on the Splunk platform with capabilities (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/administer/manage-users-and-security/10.4/manage-splunk-platform-users-and-roles/define-roles-on-the-splunk-platform-with-capabilities), and About the search language (https://help.splunk.com/en/splunk-enterprise/search/search-manual/10.4/search-overview/about-the-search-language) in the Splunk documentation.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-76538
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.16, a user who does not hold the "admin" or "power" Splunk roles could cause Splunk Enterprise to run arbitrary Search Processing Language (SPL) searches with elevated privileges through data model acceleration.
The vulnerability is possible because Splunk Enterprise does not correctly neutralize caller-supplied data model acceleration values before it places them into generated summarization searches.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-76533
CVE.report.description:
In Splunk Enterprise versions below 10.4.5, 10.2.9, 10.0.12, and 9.4.17 on Ubuntu and AlmaLinux, an unauthenticated user who obtains a valid Splunk Web session cookie before the affected user logs out could continue using the cookie after logout to access data and perform actions available to that user.
The vulnerability is possible because the logout flow does not invalidate the associated session token on affected deployments.
The attacker must obtain the valid session cookie before the affected user logs out of Splunk Web. The issue was reproduced in Splunk Enterprise installations on Ubuntu and AlmaLinux.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-132079
CVE.report.description:
Insufficient Session Expiration vulnerability in the Apache Iggy Go SDK. The TCP client method CreatePersonalAccessToken wrote the 32-bit expiry into the upper half of the 64-bit expiry field that the server reads. The server read a nonzero expiry as 2^32 times the requested value. A token created through the Go TCP client therefore stayed valid about four billion times longer than the caller asked for.

This issue affects Apache Iggy Go SDK: from 0.5.0 before 0.10.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue. Tokens that an earlier version created keep their long expiry on the server. Delete those tokens and create new ones.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129705
CVE.report.description:
In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, a broker with a listener that is configured to use the PROXY protocol v2 is vulnerable to an untrusted proxy providing details that cause the broker to accept fake SSL information.



This can be mitigated by following the documented requirements for PROXY listeners: It is very important that only trusted proxies are allowed to connect to any listener using the PROXY protocol, and that clients are not allowed to connect to the listener at all.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129149
CVE.report.description: In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, using the mosquitto_ctrl utility in interactive shell mode to interact with a malicious server could result in a crash of the utility if the server sent a hostile response.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-126763
CVE.report.description: In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 1.6 to 2.0.22 and 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, an MQTT v5.0 client connecting with a will-delay-interval that subsequently disconnects with a shorter interval causes all delayed wills to be suppressed.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-126708
CVE.report.description: In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.0.0 to 2.0.22 and 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, the return value of password hash functions for sha512-pbkdf2 and legacy sha512 were not checked. Starting with OpenSSL 4.0, sha512-pbkdf2 hashing will fail when using the FIPS provider for passwords shorter than 8 characters. This has the effect that newly created passwords would match against any other password with fewer than 8 characters.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-126706
CVE.report.description: In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1.0 to 2.1.2, the mosquitto_ctrl utility would crash if attempting to interact with a hostile broker and the broker sent a non-string "error" value.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-121482
CVE.report.description: Verifying a maliciously crafted CMS or PKCS#7 SignedData message with CRL checking enabled may consume excessive CPU time, growing with the square of the message size.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-121481
CVE.report.description: Calling EVP_EncodeBlock() with an input length close to INT_MAX may overflow the calculation of the encoded output size and write past the end of the caller-supplied output buffer.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-118493
CVE.report.description:
Insertion of Sensitive Information into Log File vulnerability in the Apache Iggy server. If Apache Iggy 0.9.0 started without IGGY_ROOT_USERNAME and IGGY_ROOT_PASSWORD, it generated a root password and wrote it to the server log file, which is enabled by default. The system snapshot command (GetSnapshot on the binary transports and POST /snapshot on HTTP) let a user with only the read_servers permission download the server log files. That user could read the generated root password and log in as root.

This issue affects Apache Iggy: 0.9.0.

Users are recommended to upgrade to version 0.10.0, which fixes the issue. Version 0.10.0 never generates a root password, and the snapshot requires the manage_servers permission. If a 0.9.0 server generated its root password, change that password.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-115107
CVE.report.description: Vulnerability in the Oracle Hyperion Planning product of Oracle Hyperion (component: Security).   The supported version that is affected is 11.2.26.0.000. Easily exploitable vulnerability allows low privileged attacker with network access via HTTP to compromise Oracle Hyperion Planning.  Successful attacks require human interaction from a person other than the attacker and while the vulnerability is in Oracle Hyperion Planning, attacks may significantly impact additional products (scope change). Successful attacks of this vulnerability can result in  unauthorized update, insert or delete access to some of Oracle Hyperion Planning accessible data as well as  unauthorized read access to a subset of Oracle Hyperion Planning accessible data. CVSS 3.1 Base Score 5.4 (Confidentiality and Integrity impacts).  CVSS Vector: (CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:L/I:L/A:N).

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-110486
CVE.report.description: In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1 through 2.1.2, a listener configured with `protocol websockets` mishandles empty WebSocket data frames. `net__read_ws()` in `lib/net_ws.c` returns the number of framing bytes consumed (the 4 masking-key bytes) for a data frame with a zero-length payload, without writing any bytes to the caller’s buffer. The MQTT packet reader in `packet__read_single()` (`lib/packet_mosq.c`) trusts that return value as a payload byte count. A remote client can therefore advance the read position over an uninitialised heap allocation, causing the broker to process and forward uninitialised heap memory (information disclosure, including heap and libc pointers), and can underflow the unsigned `to_process` counter so that subsequent attacker-controlled frame data is written past the end of the allocation (heap out-of-bounds write). The out-of-bounds write is reachable from the CONNECT packet before any authentication check, so an unauthenticated client can corrupt the heap and crash the broker even when `allow_anonymous false` is set. Combining the disclosure and the write allows remote code execution as the broker’s user by any client able to establish a session.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-107494

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-133221
CVE.report.description: A flaw was found in Keycloak. An authenticated remote user with a pending required security action, such as configuring multi-factor authentication (MFA), can bypass the mandatory action by submitting a specially crafted request to the consent endpoint without a valid session code. Keycloak incorrectly interprets the submission as a page refresh and completes the authentication process, allowing the user to access the application without fulfilling the required security policies.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-130811
CVE.report.description: @fastify/static is the Fastify plugin for serving static files. In versions up to and including 10.1.11, when it is configured to deny or ignore dotfiles together with directory listing enabled, a request for a denied dot-directory returns its directory listing instead of being refused. The underlying send step answers with a forbidden response, but the listing fallback misreads that response on a path ending in a slash as a directory without an index file and serves the listing anyway. An unauthenticated client can enumerate the names of files and subdirectories, recursively, inside dot-directories the operator explicitly denied, such as version control, backup, and key file names. File contents remain protected and only names are disclosed. The issue is fixed in @fastify/static 10.1.12, and users should upgrade to 10.1.12 or later. As a workaround, disable directory listing or do not serve a root that contains dot-directories.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-22308
CVE.report.description:
The preview mode of the OPC (OnPage Composer) page
builder of JTL-Shop is activated by a request parameter alone and
renders page data supplied in the request without checking for an authenticated
backend session with the corresponding permission. Several portlet properties

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129233
CVE.report.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 until 3.10.4, StreamBackedCorpusView performs os.stat on a caller-supplied plain string path during construction before pathsec containment is enforced. The PathPointer branch used by in-tree corpus readers is validated, so exploitation requires application code to pass an attacker-influenced string directly to the public constructor. That string can identify an out-of-root path and disclose its existence, size, and modification time even though opening the file would be rejected. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129231
CVE.report.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, SeekableUnicodeStreamReader.readline appends each new block to a growing character buffer and reruns splitlines over the entire buffer on every iteration. An attacker-controlled corpus file containing one very long unterminated line therefore causes quadratic CPU consumption in line-oriented corpus readers and can deny service. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129230
CVE.report.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, WordNet Synset.max_depth, min_depth, hypernym_paths, and hypernym_distances recursively follow attacker-controlled corpus pointers without a visited-node set or depth cap. A cyclic or excessively deep hypernym graph can raise RecursionError and terminate traversal APIs and similarity operations that depend on them. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129229
CVE.report.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 until 3.10.4, TokenSearcher.findall and Text.findall accept caller-controlled regular expressions with an unbounded number of capturing groups throughout the affected range. Starting in 3.10.3, nltk.redos.compile and RegexpTokenizer expose the same compile-time vector. The third-party regex engine compiles group-dense patterns with roughly quadratic cost before the match-time timeout begins, allowing a small unauthenticated request to exhaust CPU and deny service. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129227
CVE.report.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, Tree.fromlist recursively converts nested Python list input into Tree objects without enforcing a maximum tree depth. An attacker-controlled list nested beyond the interpreter recursion limit can raise RecursionError and terminate the current parse operation or request worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129226
CVE.report.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, the semantic-logic read_type parser recursively processes both halves of nested complex type strings without applying LogicParser.MAX_PARSE_DEPTH. An attacker-controlled type string or signature with excessive nesting can raise RecursionError through Type.fromstring or type-checking entry points and abort the current worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129225
CVE.report.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. In 3.10.3 and earlier, DependencyGraph._tree and triples recurse once per dependency edge without a depth bound, and get_cycle_path also lacks a visited-set termination guard. A deeply chained or cyclic attacker-controlled CoNLL or Malt-TAB dependency structure can raise RecursionError and abort a parse worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129223
CVE.report.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, WordNet Synset.tree and acyclic_tree traverse relation graphs through recursive utility helpers without a depth bound. Exploitation requires the host application to load an attacker-influenced custom or foreign WordNet-format lexical resource; no relation in NLTK's bundled WordNet 3.0 corpus reaches the crash threshold. An excessively deep relation graph in such a resource can exceed the Python recursion limit and terminate the traversal or request worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129222
CVE.report.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, DependencyGraph.tree and DependencyGraph.triples walk parsed dependency edges through unbounded Python recursion and do not use a working cycle or depth guard. A crafted CoNLL or Malt-TAB dependency file containing a sufficiently long chain can raise RecursionError when the documented traversal APIs are called, aborting the current worker. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129221
CVE.report.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. Prior to 3.10.4, nltk.classify.weka.ARFF_Formatter writes attacker-controlled class labels into the Weka ARFF @ATTRIBUTE '-label-' declaration without safely formatting the label tokens. Crafted labels can alter the generated ARFF schema or records, corrupting classifier input and causing integrity loss or processing failure. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

CVE.report.description:
Improper certificate validation vulnerability in Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) libdigidocpp, Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) DigiDoc4, and Estonian Information System Authority (RIA) DigiDoc on Android and iOS.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-128140
CVE.report.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.6.7 until 3.10.4, nltk.downloader follows collection membership without tracking already visited collection nodes. A self-referencing or mutually referencing collection index can therefore make the package-closure walk loop indefinitely while its queue and memory usage grow, denying service when a victim processes the attacker-influenced index. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-128139
CVE.report.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.6 to 3.10.3, XMLCorpusView._read_xml_fragment accumulates 1 KiB blocks and repeatedly applies whole-buffer XML validation while a comment or CDATA terminator remains ahead. A large comment in an attacker-controlled corpus file causes quadratic CPU consumption through documented XML corpus readers across the affected range. On 3.6 and 3.9.2, a large CDATA section incurs the quadratic scan before rejection, while on 3.10.3 both comment and CDATA documents are read successfully. This vulnerability is fixed in 3.10.4.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-128138
CVE.report.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.3 until 3.10.4, the NLTK 3.10.3 JVM hardening validates Java launcher tokens in the options channel but appends the caller-controlled cmd sequence without requiring its first token to be a main class. Supplying -jar or an @argfile through nltk.internals.java or StanfordSegmenter.java_class can therefore execute attacker-selected Java bytecode without the unsafe-JAR opt-in. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-128136
CVE.report.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.10.0 until 3.10.4, allowlisted_pickle_load keys dangerous NumPy globals by export name, allowing submodule-local numpy.lib file input/output callables to evade the denylist under the broad module allowance used by TransitionParser. A crafted pickle can invoke recfromtxt to read a local file or open_memmap to create or truncate an attacker-selected file when a victim loads an untrusted model. This issue is fixed in version 3.10.4.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-128135
CVE.report.description: NLTK (Natural Language Toolkit) is a suite of open source Python modules, data sets, and tutorials supporting research and development in Natural Language Processing. From 3.9.4 to 3.10.3, NLTK ZIP package extraction can write through an existing in-root hardlink whose other link points outside the NLTK data root. A local attacker who can prepare the extraction target can cause a package member write to overwrite an out-of-root file, violating the pathsec containment boundary and affecting integrity and availability. This issues is fixed in version 3.10.4.

A remote attacker can send HTTP requests without authentication to retrieve system configuration information, including usernames and display names, multifactor authentication configuration status, session settings, application version information, server details, hardware module firmware versions, and the BACnet/IP port used by the installation.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-133323
CVE.report.description: A vulnerability in the Audio, Web, and Video Conferencing (AWV) component of Mitel MiCollab through 10.3 (10.3.0.18) could allow an unauthenticated attacker to conduct a blind command injection attack due to insufficient parameter sanitization. A successful exploit could allow an attacker to execute arbitrary commands within the context of the system. This is MTLVULN-1864.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-133189
CVE.report.description: A command injection vulnerability was found in OpenStack Cinder's SSH-based storage-driver support. Incomplete validation of shell metacharacters allows an authenticated user who owns a volume on an affected backend to supply crafted connection information and inject additional commands into the storage array's management interface. Commands execute with the privileges of Cinder's configured backend account. This can disclose storage configuration information and, where that account has administrative permissions, could allow changes that affect the integrity or availability of other tenants' storage.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-131610
CVE.report.description:

2026.11, a condition in Web Control Center (WCC2) authorization handling could
allow an authenticated contact user to access information associated with other

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129289
CVE.report.description:
PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body.

PHP does not discard the unread part of an HTTP request body at request shutdown when the application has opened php://input without reading it to the end. When the front end reuses backend connections, which is not the default in nginx or Apache (for example nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, or Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on), PHP-FPM can parse the leftover bytes as a new FastCGI request. An unauthenticated remote attacker can use a single crafted multipart/form-data request to forge a backend request with chosen parameters such as SCRIPT_FILENAME, REMOTE_ADDR and PHP_ADMIN_VALUE, which can lead to execution of attacker-controlled PHP code. With LSAPI, subsequent requests on the connection can be disrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.2.* before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-129034
CVE.report.description: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') vulnerability in WP Chill Strong Testimonials strong-testimonials allows Stored XSS.This issue affects Strong Testimonials: from n/a through 3.3.18.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-126714
CVE.report.description:
Partially overwritten session files can lead to remote code execution.

The files session save handler, which is the default, writes updated session data into the existing session file without first clearing it. If a write is interrupted, the file can contain the beginning of the new session followed by the end of the old one, and bytes of an ordinary string can later be unserialized as objects. An attacker who can influence the session data, for example through session upload progress, and interrupt a write at a suitable point may inject objects, which can lead to code execution when the application contains a suitable gadget chain. Session data can also be corrupted.

This issue affects PHP versions 8.2.* before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120255
CVE.report.description: InfoScan uses hard-coded cryptographic keys and initialization-vector values in its database-encryption implementation. The application uses these values to encrypt the MongoDB password before storing it in the Windows registry. Because the cryptographic material is embedded in the distributed application, an individual with access to the encrypted registry value and the application code may be able to recover the database password.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-120157
CVE.report.description: The publicly distributed InfoScan Electron installer contains configuration files identifying hostnames associated with customer installations and internal development, testing, and database infrastructure. An individual who obtains and inspects the installer can extract these hostnames without authenticating to the affected systems.

CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-117659
CVE.report.description: The InfoScan Electron desktop client improperly handles TLS certificate errors by accepting certificates without validating their trustworthiness. The client also configures Electron with nodeIntegration enabled, contextIsolation disabled, and webSecurity disabled. These settings weaken the client’s security boundaries. CVE.report.title: CVE-2026-115515
CVE.report.description: @fastify/static is the Fastify plugin for serving static files. In versions before 10.1.8, the allowedPath guard receives only the requested pathname, but the underlying send step selects the file to serve afterwards, so a request for a directory resolves to its default index file and an extensionless request resolves through the configured extensions to a matching file. The selected file is streamed without being re-checked against allowedPath, so a guard that denies a specific file is bypassed by requesting its directory or extensionless form. An unauthenticated client can read files inside the static root that the application meant to keep private whenever the denied file is reachable as a directory index or an extension match. The issue is fixed in @fastify/static 10.1.8, and users should upgrade to 10.1.8 or later. As a workaround, also deny the directory and extensionless forms in allowedPath, or disable the index and extensions options.

cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-133476
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 1 hour, 40 minutes ago
Description :In Dolibarr before 24.0.3, dolForgeSQLCriteriaCallback() in htdocs/core/lib/functions.lib.php allows account takeover because it strips only a single table-name prefix from a Universal Search Filter (sqlfilters) operand before checking it against the forbidden-field denylist (pass, pass_crypted, api_key). MariaDB and MySQL accept a two-level qualification such as schema.alias.column, so an operand of the form dolibarr.u.pass_crypted survives the check and is emitted into the WHERE clause. A remote authenticated user holding only the holiday read and readall permissions, which confer no user-management or administrative access, can use the resulting boolean oracle at GET /api/index.php/holidays to recover any user's bcrypt password hash and api_key one character at a time, including an administrator's. Because api_key is accepted directly by the REST API as a bearer credential, this yields full administrative control of the application. This bypasses the fix for CVE-2026-89012, which added only a strtolower() call and did not address prefix depth. The same denylist also omits pass_temp, which stores a password in cleartext, as well as national_registration_number, salary, birth, address, personal_mobile and note_private.

cvefeed.io Latest.description:

Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 8:09 a.m. | 47 minutes ago
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ipv6: raw: fix use-after-free in rawv6_send_hdrinc() rawv6_send_hdrinc() caches the route before handing the skb to l3mdev_ip6_out(). The VRF output path may replace skb->dst and release the original route, leaving the cached pointer stale. The function later dereferences that pointer for statistics accounting and as the output device passed to NF_HOOK(). Reload the route from the current skb destination after l3mdev_ip6_out() returns. KASAN reports a slab-use-after-free in rawv6_sendmsg(), with the route allocated by ip6_dst_alloc(), freed by dst_destroy() from rcu_core(), and the related RCU callback queued from vrf_l3_out().

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-117678 - idna: punycode labels are decoded before the 63-octet length check, so a long xn-- label causes super-linear CPU use
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-117678
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 6:16 a.m. | 2 hours, 41 minutes ago
Description :Inefficient Algorithmic Complexity vulnerability in benoitc idna allows an attacker who controls a hostname passed to the library to exhaust CPU via an over-long xn-- label. idna:ulabel/1 in src/idna.erl hands every ASCII label that starts with xn-- to punycode:decode/1 without applying check_label_length/1, the 63-octet DNS label limit. punycode:decode/1 in src/punycode.erl builds its output with list appends in insert/4, so its cost grows super-linearly with the label length. A label of a few kilobytes keeps a scheduler busy for seconds to minutes before the label is rejected as invalid punycode. Every decode entry point reaches this path: decode/1, decode/2, to_unicode/1 and from_ascii/1. The encode path reaches it as well, because alabel/1 calls ulabel/1 on an ASCII xn-- label before its own length check, so encode/1, encode/2 and to_ascii/1 are affected for such input. This issue affects idna: from 0.5.0 before 8.0.0.
Severity: 6.9 | MEDIUM
Visit the link for more details, such as CVSS details, affected products, timeline, and more...

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-109555 - WP STAGING <= 4.17.0 and WP STAGING Pro <= 6.17.0 - Authenticated (Subscriber+) PHP Object Injection to Remote Code Execution via Database Restore and Staging Reset
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-109555
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 6:16 a.m. | 2 hours, 41 minutes ago
Description :The WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0 and 6.17.0, respectively, via deserialization of untrusted input during database restore and staging reset. This is due to the database importer treating attacker-controlled text beginning with {WPSTG_BINARY} as trusted internal binary data and decoding its hexadecimal suffix into serialized bytes. This makes it possible for authenticated attackers, with Subscriber-level access and above, to plant a malicious serialized object in their own profile. When an Administrator later performs an ordinary database-including restore or staging reset containing that value, and the restored profile metadata is loaded, either during the restore or in a later request, a built-in POP chain can be used to execute arbitrary code on the server. Additional built-in gadget chains allow arbitrary local file read in both WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro and arbitrary file deletion in WP STAGING Pro. The attacker does not require Administrator credentials or a copy of a backup, but exploitation does require the later privileged restore or reset.
Severity: 8.0 | HIGH

cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-99319 - ALSA: usx2y: Refuse a retried DSP load after a failure
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99319
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 8:42 a.m. | 44 minutes ago
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: usx2y: Refuse a retried DSP load after a failure snd_usx2y_hwdep_dsp_load() sets up the asynchronous sequence URBs and the interrupt URB when the FPGA firmware image with index 1 is loaded, and then creates the ALSA devices. If usx2y_in04_init() or usx2y_create_alsa_devices() fails, the URBs that were already set up are left in place. The core keeps the index unloaded when the callback fails, so user space may issue the same request again. The second attempt then enters usx2y_async_seq04_init() or usx2y_in04_init() with the URBs still allocated and trips WARN_ON(usx2y->as04.buffer) or WARN_ON(usx2y->in04_urb). The URBs cannot be released at this point: the card may already have registered PCM devices that user space can still open, and the disconnect handler accesses the URBs without holding the DSP lock. Mark the chip as hung instead, so that a retried request is refused with -ENODEV and the assertions keep their meaning. The URBs are released by snd_usx2y_card_private_free() when the card is freed. A failing usx2y_async_seq04_init() still releases its own URBs, so that path remains retryable.

cvefeed.io Latest.description:

Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 8:42 a.m. | 44 minutes ago
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: bcd2000: Fix use-after-free of MIDI URBs on file close bcd2000_disconnect() calls snd_card_disconnect(), which only prevents new opens, and then frees the MIDI URBs. The URB then stays valid until usb_put_urb() after usb_kill_urb() has returned, even if a disconnect frees it in the meantime. usb_kill_urb() itself cannot run under midi_lock, as the completion handler takes the same lock.

Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: ALSA: hwdep: Serialize DSP load requests The check of the loaded DSP indices and the call of the driver's dsp_load callback in snd_hwdep_dsp_load() are not serialized. cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99313
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 8:42 a.m. | 44 minutes ago
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: HID: logitech-hidpp: fix race condition when accessing stale stack pointer The driver uses hidpp->send_receive_buf to point to a stack-allocated buffer in the synchronous command path (__do_hidpp_send_message_sync). cvefeed.io Latest.title: CVE-2026-99312 - KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT
cvefeed.io Latest.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-99312
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 8:42 a.m. | 44 minutes ago
Description :In the Linux kernel, the following vulnerability has been resolved: KVM: x86: Unconditionally reset MMU context when emulating INIT Force an MMU reset when emulating an INIT even if paging was already disabled, as the MMU page role includes guest_mode (L2), i.e. an INIT while L2 is running with CR0.PG=0 will result in KVM running L1 with a stale MMU context. Alternatively, the reset could be scoped strictly to paging being enabled or L2 being active, but SMM is also encoded in the page role. Even though it _should_ be impossible for the vCPU to be INIT'd while SMM is active, there's zero value in not handling SMM. At that point, the only scenario where KVM _doesn't_ need to reset the MMU context is on an INIT with the vCPU running in Real Mode or Unpaged Protect Mode, and while INIT in those modes is somewhat common, it's far from a hot path and re-initializing the MMU is not expensive, especially when the role isn't changing (KVM elides most of the re-configuration in that case). Note, like the Fixes commit, this bug only affects nested SVM as INIT is an unconditional intercept on VMX, i.e. it's impossible to emulate INIT while L2 is active. Temporarily keep the guest TLB flush when CR0.PG is being cleared even though it is fully redundant with the flush that is emitted on all INIT events (KVM itself only does RESET when a vCPU is being created, i.e. when CR0.PG must be '0').

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-133476 - Dolibarr SQL Injection Vulnerability
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-133476
Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 10:18 p.m. | 2 hours, 32 minutes ago
Description :In Dolibarr before 24.0.3, dolForgeSQLCriteriaCallback() in htdocs/core/lib/functions.lib.php allows account takeover because it strips only a single table-name prefix from a Universal Search Filter (sqlfilters) operand before checking it against the forbidden-field denylist (pass, pass_crypted, api_key). MariaDB and MySQL accept a two-level qualification such as schema.alias.column, so an operand of the form dolibarr.u.pass_crypted survives the check and is emitted into the WHERE clause. A remote authenticated user holding only the holiday read and readall permissions, which confer no user-management or administrative access, can use the resulting boolean oracle at GET /api/index.php/holidays to recover any user's bcrypt password hash and api_key one character at a time, including an administrator's. Because api_key is accepted directly by the REST API as a bearer credential, this yields full administrative control of the application. This bypasses the fix for CVE-2026-89012, which added only a strtolower() call and did not address prefix depth. The same denylist also omits pass_temp, which stores a password in cleartext, as well as national_registration_number, salary, birth, address, personal_mobile and note_private.
Severity: 8.8 | HIGH

Description :Etherpad is a real-time collaborative editor. Description :Timezone cache use-after-free can lead to remote code execution. In non-thread-safe builds, a diagnostic written to a file-based error_log during module startup, for example for an invalid date.timezone value or a session configuration warning, causes the timezone cache to be allocated in startup memory that is freed while a reference to it is kept. Published : Nov. 19, 2026, 3:17 p.m. | 1 hour, 33 minutes ago
Description :PHP-FPM request smuggling through an unread HTTP request body. PHP does not discard the unread part of an HTTP request body at request shutdown when the application has opened php://input without reading it to the end. When the front end reuses backend connections, which is not the default in nginx or Apache (for example nginx with fastcgi_keep_conn on, or Apache mod_proxy_fcgi with enablereuse=on), PHP-FPM can parse the leftover bytes as a new FastCGI request. With LSAPI, subsequent requests on the connection can be disrupted. This issue affects PHP versions 8.2.* before 8.2.36, 8.3.* before 8.3.37, 8.4.* before 8.4.28 and 8.5.* before 8.5.13.

Description :The WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro plugins for WordPress are vulnerable to PHP Object Injection in all versions up to, and including, 4.17.0 and 6.17.0, respectively, via deserialization of untrusted input during database restore and staging reset. This is due to the database importer treating attacker-controlled text beginning with {WPSTG_BINARY} as trusted internal binary data and decoding its hexadecimal suffix into serialized bytes. Additional built-in gadget chains allow arbitrary local file read in both WP STAGING and WP STAGING Pro and arbitrary file deletion in WP STAGING Pro. The attacker does not require Administrator credentials or a copy of a backup, but exploitation does require the later privileged restore or reset.

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-130001 - Mustache Ruby Server-Side Template Injection Remote Code Execution
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-130001
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 4:28 p.m. | 2 hours, 39 minutes ago
Description :> [!NOTE] > The vulnerability was fully disclosed to the maintainer in private prior to security advisories were enabled for the project. > This advisory presents a limited information for initial release to provide a time window for installing updates. Full information with PoCs would be added later. ## Summary Mustache template engine for Ruby in versions 1.1.2 and earlier allows remote attackers to achieve arbitrary code execution through accessing specific built-in methods in an attacker-supplied template. ## Details Mustache is often suggested as a safe simple template language to avoid SSTI vulnerabilities.[^1] [^2] Mustache for Ruby up to version 1.1.2 did not properly restrict method access which allowed chaining multiple built-in methods to achieve arbitrary code execution. > [!IMPORTANT] > Successful exploitation of this vulnerability does not depend on any configuration or objects passed to the template engine. > An attacker controlling the template string can achieve arbitrary code execution without any additional requirements. Additional methods provided by the application or installed gems can further expand the attack surface but exploitation was proven without them. ## PoC All discovered payloads were tested using `ruby -e` shell commands with `mustache` as the only explicitly required gem: ```bash ruby -e 'require "mustache"; puts Mustache.render("PAYLOAD GOES HERE", key: "value")' ``` For initial information release, only the descriptions of the most important discovered payloads would be provided: - Universal RCE for a major Ruby version - File upload to RCE (3 different payloads) - Infinite memory consumption DoS - Infinite sleep DoS Universal RCE payloads for other major Ruby versions and other payloads could exist, as the attack surface is very large. The presented list only contains payloads discovered using a fairly primitive approach. > [!CAUTION] > Exploitation is not limited to the discovered Exploits/PoCs and real-life web applications are likely to expose even more dangerous functionality. ## Impact An attacker with the ability to modify the template string can execute arbitrary code in the context of the Ruby application. ## Rationale for CVSS assessment: - Attack Vector: Network > No network requirements are present for exploitation. > Templating functionality is often provided on public websites. - Attack Complexity: Low > Attacker can expect reliable and repeatable exploitation. > There are no requirements beyond attacker's control. - Privileges Required: None > Mustache is often used for untrusted user-supplied templates. > Exploitation is often possible without authorization or by using self-registered accounts (without prior privileges). > Mustache by itself does not provide access control functionality. - User Interaction: None > Exploitation does not require any user interaction to achieve RCE. - Scope: Unchanged > The code is executed with the same privileges as the web application, without changing the scope. - Confidentiality Impact: High > Arbitrary code execution leads to the total loss of confidentiality. - Integrity Impact: High > Arbitrary code execution leads to the total loss of integrity. - Availability Impact: High > Arbitrary code execution can be used to achieve the total loss of availability. ## Resources [^1]: https://portswigger.net/knowledgebase/papers/serversidetemplateinjection.pdf [^2]: https://hackerone.com/reports/423541

cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-110486 - Remote heap out-of-bounds read/write in Eclipse Mosquitto
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-110486
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 10:15 a.m. | 18 minutes ago
Description :In Eclipse Mosquitto versions 2.1 through 2.1.2, a listener configured with `protocol websockets` mishandles empty WebSocket data frames. `net__read_ws()` in `lib/net_ws.c` returns the number of framing bytes consumed (the 4 masking-key bytes) for a data frame with a zero-length payload, without writing any bytes to the caller’s buffer. The MQTT packet reader in `packet__read_single()` (`lib/packet_mosq.c`) trusts that return value as a payload byte count. A remote client can therefore advance the read position over an uninitialised heap allocation, causing the broker to process and forward uninitialised heap memory (information disclosure, including heap and libc pointers), and can underflow the unsigned `to_process` counter so that subsequent attacker-controlled frame data is written past the end of the allocation (heap out-of-bounds write). The out-of-bounds write is reachable from the CONNECT packet before any authentication check, so an unauthenticated client can corrupt the heap and crash the broker even when `allow_anonymous false` is set. Combining the disclosure and the write allows remote code execution as the broker’s user by any client able to establish a session.
Severity: 9.8 | CRITICAL

The issue has been fixed in Airlock Gateway version 8.5.3 and 8.6.1. For an attack to be executable, the Airlock Gateway needs to have 'Smart Form Protection' (or the corresponding expert settings) enabled on a mapping whose backend returns a response containing certain multi-byte HTML character references. cvefeed.io High & Critical.title: CVE-2026-105929 - Ansible-core: ansible-galaxy role install path traversal via unvalidated role name allows file writes and directory deletion outside the roles directory
cvefeed.io High & Critical.description:
CVE ID :CVE-2026-105929
Published : Nov. 18, 2026, 1:58 a.m. | 19 minutes ago
Description :A path traversal vulnerability (CWE-22) was found in ansible-core's ansible-galaxy role installation. An explicit role "name" taken from a role's meta/requirements.yml is used to construct the on-disk installation path without validating that the resulting destination stays within the selected roles directory. A name containing "../" escapes that directory, and an absolute name replaces it entirely. Because ansible-galaxy processes transitive dependencies from an installed role's meta/requirements.yml, a malicious role publisher can cause attacker-supplied files to be written outside the operator's chosen roles directory when the operator installs the role, and, when --force is used, can cause an existing role directory outside that path to be removed and replaced. The impact is bounded by the invoking user's filesystem permissions and requires the operator to install the attacker-influenced content.
Severity: 8.1 | HIGH

Description :Philips Hue Bridge HomeKit Accessory Protocol chacha20_decrypt Integer Underflow Remote Code Execution Vulnerability. Full Disclosure.title: Open WebUI: the Windows installer mints the master key from the install second — CVE-2025-15603 was rejected; here is the measurement
Full Disclosure.description:
Posted by theknell--- via Fulldisclosure on Nov 12

Open WebUI's Windows installer (start_windows.bat) generates
WEBUI_SECRET_KEY — the master secret that signs every session token —
from the C library's rand(), a linear congruential generator seeded
once with the current time in seconds. The key's entire entropy is
the second in which the software was installed.

From any ordinary user's own token, the master key is recoverable
blind in ~2.1 seconds across a ±1-day...

FortiGuard Outbreak Alerts.description:
Threat actors are targeting internet-accessible refrigeration management interfaces and industrial temperature controllers, exploiting vulnerabilities, authentication weaknesses and insecure configurations to gain unauthorized access.

The affected technologies include:

- Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC refrigeration controllers.
- Copeland XWEB refrigeration management systems.
- Dixell XWEB remote monitoring systems.
- Other remotely accessible industrial refrigeration and temperature-control equipment.

Following successful access, attackers can manipulate refrigeration configurations, including temperature setpoints, defrost schedules and operating parameters.

These changes can force refrigeration equipment into continuous heating or defrost cycles, resulting in elevated temperatures, spoiled food and other temperature-sensitive products, equipment damage, operational disruption and potential fire hazards.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Java4Shell
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

CVE-2026-114938, known as Java4Shell, is a critical heap-based buffer overflow vulnerability in the Base64 implementation of the Java standard library.

The vulnerability affects Java runtimes on systems using x86-64 processors that support AVX-512 Vector Byte Manipulation Instructions (VBMI). An unauthenticated remote attacker could potentially exploit the flaw by sending specially crafted Base64 data to vulnerable Java processes, resulting in memory corruption, information disclosure, application crashes, or arbitrary code execution.

The vulnerability occurs when the Java Base64 implementation processes specially crafted input using an optimized AVX-512 code path.

An invalid condition in the processing logic can cause data to be written beyond the bounds of an internal eight-byte buffer, potentially corrupting adjacent memory.

Depending on the application and execution environment, successful exploitation could result in:
- Arbitrary code execution within the affected Java process.
- Disclosure of sensitive information from process memory.
- Memory corruption and application crashes.
- Potential compromise of applications and services running vulnerable Java environments.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Organizations are advised to review the Oracle Security Alerts for the latest vulnerability details, affected versions, and available patches.

On November 17, 2026, CISA issued an alert urging organizations to immediately patch CVE-2026-114938 (Java4Shell).

CISA recommends identifying vulnerable Java installations, including runtimes embedded in third-party applications, containers, and appliances, and prioritizing remediation of internet-facing systems. Where patching is not immediately possible, organizations should implement temporary mitigations, including restricting and validating Base64 input and limiting unauthenticated access.

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: Apache HTTP/2 RCE
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

CVE-2026-119618 is a race condition (CWE-362) in Apache HTTP Server's mod_http2 module. In assign_headers(), the module writes to a header table that is shared between the connection thread and worker threads without adequate synchronization. Concurrent access can corrupt the Apache child-process heap, which can be leveraged toward remote code execution in the worker process.

Exploitation requires no authentication and no user interaction. The server only reaches the vulnerable code when HTTP/2 is enabled through the Protocols directive (h2 or h2c). The Apache default is HTTP/1.1, which is not exposed.

Apache HTTP Server is one of the most widely deployed web servers, and this flaw is reachable by an unauthenticated attacker over the network on any instance with HTTP/2 enabled.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Affected versions:
• Apache HTTP Server 2.4.55 through 2.4.70, when HTTP/2 is enabled.
• Standalone mod_h2 2.0.8 through 2.0.42.

1. Apply the security update. Upgrade to Apache HTTP Server 2.4.71 or later, or install the distribution vendor's fixed package, then restart httpd. Prioritize internet-facing servers with HTTP/2 enabled.

2. Confirm exposure. Check whether mod_http2 is loaded (apachectl -M | grep http2) and whether any Protocols directive includes h2 or h2c, globally or per virtual host. Servers without HTTP/2 are not affected.

3. If patching is delayed, set Protocols http/1.1 and check every virtual host. This removes exposure but is not a substitute for patching.

4. Rebuild containers. Rebuild and redeploy container images that bundle the affected Apache versions. Restarting a running container does not update the binary.

5. Standalone mod_h2 users should disable HTTP/2 until a fixed standalone release is available.

6. Monitor for signs of exploitation. Correlate HTTP/2 request bursts with Apache worker crashes, segmentation faults, or restarts. Alert on unexpected child processes spawned by httpd or apache2, and on new files in web roots or temporary directories.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: WordPress Core Time-of-check Time-of-use (TOCTOU) Race Condition Vulnerability
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Vulnerability?

CVE-2026-119977 is a time-of-check time-of-use (TOCTOU) race condition (CWE-367) in WordPress Core that affects the full-package core upgrade process. During an update, WordPress stages upgrade files in a predictable, web-accessible directory under `wp-content/upgrade/`. These files include the `setup-config.php` installer.

An unauthenticated remote attacker who accesses the staged installer during the upgrade window can exploit this condition to execute arbitrary code on the server. According to published technical analyses, the attacker can supply their own database configuration details, causing the upgrade process to overwrite the site's existing `wp-config.php` file with the attacker's configuration. This can allow the attacker to create an administrator account and execute arbitrary PHP code.

The vulnerability has a CVSS score of 8.1. Exploitation requires no authentication or user interaction but is timing-dependent, as the attack is only possible while a vulnerable site is actively performing a full-package core update.

Although the exploitation window is limited to the duration of the update process, the exposure is significant because WordPress sites are widely deployed and internet-facing. Organizations running affected versions should prioritize applying the security update and verify that no unauthorized changes or administrator accounts were introduced during potentially vulnerable upgrade windows.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

Fixed versions: WordPress released 7.1.4 on October 28, 2026, with fixes for each supported branch.

1. Block web access to wp-content/upgrade/ before updating. The first update to a fixed release still runs through the vulnerable updater. Researchers recommend denying the path at the web server (Nginx or Apache) and confirming a 403 response before starting the update.
2. Apply the security update. Upgrade to WordPress 7.1.4, or to the fixed release for your branch, then verify the installed version.
3. Clean up staging files. Delete leftover files under wp-content/upgrade/ that the updater did not remove.
4. Monitor for exploitation attempts. Review web server logs for requests to PHP files under wp-content/upgrade/, especially setup-config.php.
5. Review for compromise indicators. Check wp-config.php for unexpected changes, such as a different database host. Look for unfamiliar administrator accounts, unknown plugins, and unrecognized PHP files.
6. If compromise is suspected, restore a known-good configuration, rotate database and administrator credentials, and engage incident response.

What FortiGuard Coverage is available?

FortiGuard Labs continues to monitor exploitation attempts targeting WordPress Core and the associated attack techniques.

FortiGuard customers should use multiple layers of defense to help identify and mitigate suspicious activity associated with the exploitation of CVE-2026-119977:

FortiGuard Threat Signal.title: OT Refrigeration Control Systems Attack
FortiGuard Threat Signal.description:
What is the Attack?

November 9, 2026 Update – Threat Attribution: On November 9, 2026, France's CERT-FR published a threat intelligence report attributing the October 11–12 attacks against industrial refrigeration controllers to Shahid Kaveh, an Iranian cyber-offensive unit operating within the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps' Electronic and Cyber Center (IRGC-CEC). According to the report, the attack compromised refrigeration controllers at approximately 700 retail locations across France, modifying defrost settings to trigger high-temperature cycles, resulting in significant product losses and at least 15 reported fires. The assessment is supported by shared attack infrastructure, the use of the FOFA scanning tool, promotion of the operation through the group's CyberbanNews channel, and traces of Persian language in the attack infrastructure. CERT-FR also documents the group's broader targeting of industrial control systems, including Schneider Electric, Siemens, and Rockwell equipment, and its historical use of Modbus over TCP port 502 for industrial reconnaissance.

November 2, 2026 Update: A new wave of suspected cyberattacks has affected supermarket refrigeration systems across several European countries, including Sweden, Belgium, Luxembourg, Ireland, and Estonia. Reported incidents involved attackers manipulating refrigeration controls and triggering defrost cycles or raising temperatures, with some equipment reportedly reaching 50°C. Affected retailers include ICA, Coop, Carrefour, Delhaize, Colruyt, and SuperValu. Sweden's National Cyber Security Centre (NCSC-SE) confirmed it was responding to incidents involving ICA and Coop stores. However, authorities have not established whether these incidents are connected to the October attacks in France or share the same threat actors or infrastructure. No threat group has claimed responsibility, and no new malware or indicators of compromise have been publicly confirmed.

On October 11–12, 2026, attackers compromised refrigeration control systems at supermarkets across France, remotely manipulating refrigeration settings and triggering defrost cycles. The attacks caused temperatures in some refrigeration units to rise to as high as 50°C, resulting in food spoilage and operational disruption. Affected retailers reportedly included Intermarché, Netto, Carrefour, Coopérative U, Monoprix, and E.Leclerc.

France's national cybersecurity agency, CERT-FR, reported compromises involving Danfoss AK-SM and AK-SC controllers, as well as Copeland and Dixell XWEB systems. These systems monitor and manage commercial refrigeration and related building operations. Their compromise can allow unauthorized changes to operating parameters, potentially disrupting temperature control and damaging perishable goods.

Separate research by Claroty Team82 identified vulnerabilities affecting Danfoss AK-SM 8xxA controllers, including:
CVE-2025-41450, an authentication bypass
CVE-2025-41451, an OS command injection vulnerability that can lead to remote code execution
CVE-2025-41452, a web server configuration vulnerability that can lead to denial of service
Danfoss released fixes for the above vulnerabilities, and organizations should update affected devices to the applicable patched firmware.

Additional research by Claroty Team82 and CISA documented vulnerabilities affecting Copeland XWEB Pro controllers, including:
CVE-2026-25085, an authentication bypass
CVE-2026-21718, an authentication bypass that can enable pre-authentication code execution
CVE-2026-24663, an unauthenticated OS command injection vulnerability
The affected Copeland models include XWEB300D PRO, XWEB500D PRO, and XWEB500B PRO running firmware version 1.12.1 or earlier. Organizations should consult the vendor's remediation guidance and apply the appropriate firmware updates.

What is the recommended Mitigation?

On October 12, France's national cybersecurity response team, CERT-FR, issued alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 warning of numerous compromises involving remote refrigeration controllers.

Organizations should immediately remove direct internet exposure from refrigeration controllers and restrict remote administration to secure VPN connections or protected management networks. Review controller configurations, particularly temperature settings and defrost schedules, and apply available firmware updates and vendor-recommended security settings. Change default credentials and replace unsupported, end-of-life devices where necessary.

If compromise is suspected, isolate affected equipment and follow vendor and CERT-FR recovery guidance before restoring operations. A factory reset alone is insufficient if the device remains vulnerable and exposed. Organizations should also segment OT networks from corporate IT environments, restrict access to authorized personnel, and monitor for unexpected changes to refrigeration settings.

Danfoss identifies firmware R4.2 as the fix for CVE-2025-41450 and R4.3.1 as the fix for CVE-2025-41451 and CVE-2025-41452. Verify the correct release against the specific device model.
